senses.definition: (of a person or remark) sharp and forthright, often in a cruel way
senses.example: Her acerbic wit made her a feared critic.

senses.definition: to diminish or put at rest fear, suspicion or worry
senses.example: The doctor tried to allay her fears about the operation.

senses.definition: to state or assert to be the case
senses.example: The witness averred that she had seen the defendant at the scene.

senses.definition: to scold or criticize someone angrily
senses.example: The coach berated the team at halftime.

senses.definition: to increase the strength of or justify
senses.example: She buttressed her argument with statistics.

senses.definition: a projecting support built against a wall
senses.example: Stone buttresses hold up the cathedral's walls.

senses.definition: rude in a mean-spirited and surly way
senses.example: It would be churlish to refuse such a kind offer.

senses.definition: a sudden and ignominious failure; a fiasco
senses.example: The product launch was a debacle: nothing worked.

senses.definition: a political leader who seeks support by appealing to popular desires and prejudices rather than by using rational argument
senses.example: The demagogue blamed every problem on outsiders.

senses.definition: showing or having skill, especially with the hands
senses.example: The dexterous surgeon tied the knots in seconds.

senses.definition: to disturb the composure of; to unsettle
senses.example: The interviewer's long silences disconcerted the candidates.

senses.definition: a feeling of anxiety or worry
senses.example: The layoffs caused widespread disquiet among the staff.

senses.definition: to make someone worried or anxious
senses.example: The silence from the mountain hut disquieted the rescuers.

senses.definition: (with reference to a feeling or other intangible thing) to disappear or cause to disappear
senses.example: Her anger dissipated as she listened to his explanation.

senses.definition: to squander money, energy or resources
senses.example: He dissipated his inheritance in a few years.

senses.definition: seeking to impose a doctrine in all circumstances without regard to practical considerations
senses.example: Her doctrinaire approach left no room for compromise.

senses.definition: to declare one's public approval or support of
senses.example: The newspaper endorsed the challenger.

senses.definition: a feeling of listlessness and dissatisfaction arising from a lack of occupation or excitement
senses.example: The long winter filled him with ennui.

senses.definition: to erase or remove completely
senses.example: His conviction was expunged from the record.

senses.definition: serving to make guilt or an offense seem less serious or more forgivable
senses.example: Given the extenuating circumstances, the judge reduced the sentence.

senses.definition: to free someone or something from a constraint or difficulty
senses.example: The rescuers extricated the driver from the wreck.

senses.definition: changing frequently, especially as regards one's loyalties or affections
senses.example: The fickle public soon forgot the singer.

senses.definition: impressive or magnificent in appearance or style, especially pretentiously so
senses.example: He had grandiose plans for a theme park in the desert.

senses.definition: assuming power or authority without justification; arrogant and domineering
senses.example: Her imperious manner offended the staff.

senses.definition: intelligently analytical and clear-thinking
senses.example: Her incisive questions exposed the flaws in the plan.

senses.definition: impossible to understand or interpret
senses.example: Her inscrutable smile gave nothing away.

senses.definition: traveling from place to place
senses.example: The itinerant preacher visited a different village every week.

senses.definition: tired, bored or lacking enthusiasm, typically after having had too much of something
senses.example: Even jaded critics loved the show.

senses.definition: tending to talk a great deal; talkative
senses.example: The loquacious taxi driver told us his life story.

senses.definition: (especially of a process or organization) just coming into existence and beginning to display signs of future potential
senses.example: The nascent industry needed government support.

senses.definition: harmful, poisonous or very unpleasant
senses.example: The factory released noxious fumes.

senses.definition: to make obscure, unclear or unintelligible
senses.example: The report obfuscates the truth with jargon.

senses.definition: not aware of or not concerned about what is happening around one
senses.example: He was oblivious to the danger.

senses.definition: annoyingly insensitive or slow to understand
senses.example: He was being deliberately obtuse.

senses.definition: (of an angle) more than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees
senses.example: The triangle has one obtuse angle.

senses.definition: something that is one's duty or responsibility
senses.example: The onus is on the prosecution to prove guilt.

senses.definition: feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong
senses.example: The penitent thief returned the money.

senses.definition: relevant or applicable to a particular matter
senses.example: Please keep your questions pertinent to the topic.

senses.definition: (of a person or their manner) childishly sulky or bad-tempered
senses.example: The petulant star stormed off the set.

senses.definition: a remark or statement, especially one with a moral content, that has been used too often to be interesting or thoughtful
senses.example: The speech was full of platitudes about hard work.

senses.definition: a preference or special liking for something
senses.example: He has a predilection for spicy food.

senses.definition: remarkably or impressively great in extent, size or degree
senses.example: She had a prodigious memory for faces.

senses.definition: a cancellation or postponement of a punishment
senses.example: The prisoner was granted a reprieve.

senses.definition: to cancel or postpone the punishment of someone
senses.example: The condemned man was reprieved hours before his execution.

senses.definition: admirably purposeful, determined and unwavering
senses.example: She was resolute in her opposition to the plan.

senses.definition: the occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way
senses.example: It was pure serendipity that we met on the train.

senses.definition: having assets in excess of liabilities; able to pay one's debts
senses.example: The bank remained solvent through the crisis.

senses.definition: a liquid able to dissolve other substances
senses.example: Water is the most common solvent.

senses.definition: pretentious or juvenile
senses.example: The script was full of sophomoric humor.

senses.definition: (of a place) extremely dirty and unpleasant, especially as a result of poverty or neglect
senses.example: The family lived in a squalid apartment.

senses.definition: showing or involving a contemptible lack of moral standards
senses.example: The affair was a squalid tale of greed.

senses.definition: to supersede and replace
senses.example: Digital cameras supplanted film cameras within a decade.

senses.definition: vigorous or incisive in expression or style
senses.example: The critic's trenchant review exposed the film's weaknesses.

senses.definition: (of a person) not aware of the full facts
senses.example: She was an unwitting accomplice in the fraud.

senses.definition: not done on purpose; unintentional
senses.example: His unwitting remark revealed the surprise.

senses.definition: to take a position of power or importance illegally or by force
senses.example: The general usurped the throne.

senses.definition: accorded a great deal of respect, especially because of age, wisdom or character
senses.example: The venerable professor taught for sixty years.

senses.definition: skilled at gaining an advantage, especially deceitfully
senses.example: The wily fox outsmarted the hounds.
